clue.text: Step judge's taken over leftie oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the judge has taken the lead, so that piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: passing over the odd-numbered letters means only the evenly placed ones of the word survive

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A judge, with a left-wing colleague strangely ignored, takes a step forward in court.
explanation.walkthrough: J plus the even letters of leftie gives JETE, a ballet term.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other, so it is a kind of dance step.

clue.text: Piece from speaker I love

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone recites a passage from a speaker they adore.
explanation.walkthrough: ORATOR + I + O gives ORATORIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Court accommodating Rhode Island in review

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to a guest, so the court's letters hold the state's inside them

parts.note: CT is the usual abbreviation for court
the postal code for the US state

explanation.surface: A court in Rhode Island is under review.
explanation.walkthrough: C(RI)T gives CRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crit is informal shorthand for a critique, a critical review of a piece of work, especially in art schools.

clue.text: Arouse interest in reading device

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stir up a feeling, as one lights a fire
second meaning: Amazon's brand of e-book reader

explanation.surface: A gadget for reading is meant to spark enthusiasm for books.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is literally to light a fire and figuratively to stir up feelings; the Kindle is also a well-known electronic book reader.

clue.text: Brand — first in Scotland listener supports

only the opening letter of the place name is wanted here

the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.walkthrough: S on top of EAR gives SEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand is to burn a mark into skin with hot iron, which is to sear it.

clue.text: Person trying to find Home Counties house

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England
Sagittarius, the Archer, is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone is house-hunting in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London; 'house' here is an astrological house, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is literally one who searches, someone looking for something they hope to locate.

clue.text: Leaflet perhaps, debut for Hibs, also published

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so just the opening letter of the club name is used

parts.note: the first letter; Hibs is Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club
both join one thing to another
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A club leaflet celebrates a player's first game for Hibs, which has also been put out.
explanation.walkthrough: H + AND + OUT gives HANDOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is a printed sheet given out free, of which a leaflet is a typical example.

clue.text: One's destiny to be full of anger in French department?

indicators.note: something full of a feeling holds it within, so the fate's letters wrap round the other word

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: Someone is fated to be furious in some French government office.
explanation.walkthrough: LO(IRE)T gives LOIRET; 'department' suggests an office, but it is a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loiret is one of the administrative départements of France, around Orléans.

clue.text: City guides — audio version

indicators.note: an audio version is one that is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: one who guides others leads them

explanation.surface: A city's tour guides are now available as recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire in the north of England.

clue.text: Tidy number originally put away

indicators.note: at its origin, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter
food put away has been consumed

explanation.surface: Tidy up a figure originally filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: To put away food is informal for eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten something is to make it neat and orderly, which is to tidy it.

clue.text: Fellow's article upfront on Dunfermline's No 1 source of riches maybe

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: what is upfront is at the start, so only the leading letter of the little word after it is taken

parts.note: its first letter

indicators.note: number one means the first in line, here the opening letter of the town

parts.note: its first letter
ore is mined for precious metals

explanation.surface: A man's newspaper piece puts a Dunfermline footballer up front as a possible goldmine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upfront' covers just 'on', giving its first letter, not the article. THE + O + D + ORE gives THEODORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore is a man's first name, and a fellow is simply a man.

clue.text: Title loss? Hero needs to change pattern

indicators.note: changing the words means their letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: the fodder

clue.text: Time, hour, with former pupil — feel emotion

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
HR abbreviates hour
OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil returns to the school for an hour, feeling emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: T + HR + OB gives THROB.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart throbs with strong feeling, so to throb is to pulse with excitement or passion.

clue.text: Formula One champion's girl's from South

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting at the southern end means reading the name upwards

parts.note: Anne's, a girl's name with its possessive

explanation.surface: A racing champion's girlfriend comes from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNES read upwards gives SENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrton Senna, the Brazilian driver, was Formula One world champion three times.

clue.text: Somewhat popular, genial, generous

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part, so the answer is just a section of the following words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Describing a well-liked, friendly, open-handed person.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean liberal or open-handed, as in a large-hearted or large-minded person, so generous.

clue.text: Trunk initially dropped roughly

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word has been let fall

parts.note: the torso is the body's trunk

explanation.surface: A trunk was dropped somewhere around the start of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: TORSO without its first letter gives OR SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacked onto a number, the phrase or so means approximately, as in ten or so.

clue.text: Key boost

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a vital lift; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the tonic is the first note of a scale and names its key; a tonic is also a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Character providing introduction to further capital

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character
providing means on condition that

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the beginning, so only the word's opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.walkthrough: A card is an informal word for a comic eccentric. CARD + IF + F gives CARDIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh seat of government sits in this city, so it is an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Garment artist's returned reaching India

parts.note: RA's: an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.walkthrough: RAS reversed gives SAR, then I gives SARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long wrapped garment of cloth worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Coastal features — aquatic mammals with a large inside

taken as written

clue.text: Unusually able and accurate, welcoming a test of knowledge

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Leading couples in casual, light cotton fabric

parts.note: first two letters
first two letters
first two letters

explanation.surface: Couples at a dance wear casual light cotton outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of each of the three words give CALICO.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven cotton cloth, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Accept a woman on her wedding day has run off?

parts.note: the woman being married

explanation.walkthrough: The bride did not flee; 'run' is the R that goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate or put up with it, which is to accept it.

clue.text: With suggestion one politician not telling the truth?

parts.note: Roman numeral one
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Insinuating that a politician isn't being honest.
explanation.walkthrough: I + MP + LYING gives IMPLYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Implying means indicating something indirectly, so speaking with a hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Show behind a short time — now performing

parts.note: a mo is a moment
a show that is on is being performed now

explanation.surface: A show going on later, after a short break, is now playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show behind' looks like a show running late, but it means bare one's buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is slang for baring one's buttocks to someone as an insult or joke.

clue.text: Good Polish food

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to polish something is to rub it

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine Polish meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality, but it is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for food, a usage common in Britain.

parts.note: the fodder

clue.text: Dubious article from Paris that hurt inwardly

indicators.note: the cry of pain is placed within the French word

the exclamation one says when it hurts

clue.text: Newly influential, shunning hospital department — it's not becoming (relatively?)

parts.note: taken as written
ear, nose and throat
